## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-12-build-gene-co-expression-networks-using-hdwgcna/>

Part 2 of 2. Starting from the metacell object prepared in part 1, this
notebook builds the signed co-expression network at the chosen soft power
(`params$soft.power`), cuts the gene dendrogram into modules, computes module
eigengenes (Harmony-corrected across samples) and intramodular connectivity
(kME) to find hub genes, scores modules per cell with UCell, runs Enrichr
(optional, needs internet), tests differential module eigengenes between two
conditions, and draws hub-gene network and module UMAP plots. Results are saved
as a Seurat object and CSV files.

**Input:** `results/seurat_wgcna_prenetwork.rds` written by part 1 (itself
derived from `seurat_subset_downsampled.rds`, created by tutorial 7 part 1,
which must be run first).

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 6-14). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments. Note: the article's step headings are partly mislabelled
(several code blocks sit under the previous step's heading and there is no
"Step 9" code block); the `# STEP` banners here follow the article's h2/h3
headings.

## Libraries and data

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load Libraries and Data (from part 1)
#-----------------------------------------------
library(hdWGCNA)
library(WGCNA)
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
library(igraph)
library(enrichR)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_12_coexpression_hdwgcna/tut12_coexpression_hdwgcna_part2.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

base.dir <- params$base.dir
wgcna.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$wgcna.subdir)
for (d in c("plots", "results")) {
  dir.create(file.path(wgcna.dir, d), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

set.seed(params$seed)

celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
target.celltype <- params$target.celltype

# Enable multi-threading for WGCNA correlation computations
enableWGCNAThreads(nThreads = params$n.threads)

# ADDED: hand-off from part 1
prenet.path <- file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/seurat_wgcna_prenetwork.rds")
if (!file.exists(prenet.path)) stop("Run part 1 first: ", prenet.path, " not found.")
seurat_obj <- readRDS(prenet.path)

# ADDED: checks on what part 2 needs
stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, sample.col, condition.col) %in%
                colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)),
          params$umap.reduction %in% Reductions(seurat_obj),
          target.celltype %in% as.character(seurat_obj[[celltype.col]][, 1]),
          all(c(params$dme.group1, params$dme.group2) %in%
                as.character(seurat_obj[[condition.col]][, 1])))

soft_power <- params$soft.power
```

## Construct the co-expression network

```{r step6_network}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: Construct the Co-expression Network
#-----------------------------------------------
seurat_obj <- ConstructNetwork(
  seurat_obj,
  soft_power      = soft_power,
  setDatExpr      = FALSE,                    # SetDatExpr was already called in part 1
  networkType     = params$network.type,
  TOMType         = params$tom.type,
  minModuleSize   = params$min.module.size,   # Minimum number of genes required to form a module
  mergeCutHeight  = params$merge.cut.height   # Modules with < 25% dissimilarity are merged together
)
```

```{r step6_dendrogram}
# PlotDendrogram uses base R graphics, not ggplot -- must use pdf() on HPC
# (title derived from params; the article hard-codes "Classical Monocyte")
dendro.title <- paste(target.celltype, "hdWGCNA Dendrogram")
pdf(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/dendrogram.pdf"), width = 10, height = 5)
PlotDendrogram(seurat_obj, main = dendro.title)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: png twin so the plot shows in the rendered notebook
dendro.png <- file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/dendrogram.png")
png(dendro.png, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", res = params$plot.dpi)
PlotDendrogram(seurat_obj, main = dendro.title)
invisible(dev.off())
```

```{r step6_show_dendrogram, out.width = "90%"}
# ADDED: show the base-graphics PNG saved above
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(dendro.png))
```

## Compute module eigengenes

```{r step7_eigengenes}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 7: Compute Module Eigengenes
#-----------------------------------------------
# Scale features before computing eigengenes (required by PCA-based eigengene calculation)
# Kept as in the article. NOTE: ScaleData on VariableFeatures only scales
# those genes, while eigengenes are computed from the network genes; network
# genes that are not variable features have no scaled values. The check below
# only warns; it does not change the result.
seurat_obj <- ScaleData(seurat_obj, features = VariableFeatures(seurat_obj))

# ADDED: warn if many network genes are missing from the scaled data
scaled.genes <- tryCatch(
  rownames(GetAssayData(seurat_obj, assay = params$expr.assay, layer = "scale.data")),
  error = function(e) NULL
)
net.genes <- GetModules(seurat_obj, wgcna_name = params$wgcna.name)$gene_name
if (!is.null(scaled.genes)) {
  frac.scaled <- mean(net.genes %in% scaled.genes)
  message(sprintf("%.1f%% of network genes are in the scaled data.", 100 * frac.scaled))
  if (frac.scaled < 0.9) {
    warning("Only ", round(100 * frac.scaled, 1), "% of network genes have scaled values; ",
            "module eigengenes may use fewer genes than the network contains.")
  }
}

# Compute module eigengenes on individual cells
# group.by.vars enables Harmony correction of eigengenes across samples
seurat_obj <- ModuleEigengenes(
  seurat_obj,
  group.by.vars = sample.col  # Harmonize across biological replicates
)
```

## Compute intramodular connectivity (kME)

```{r step8_kme}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: Compute Intramodular Connectivity (kME)
#-----------------------------------------------
# Compute kME for all genes in their assigned modules
seurat_obj <- ModuleConnectivity(
  seurat_obj,
  group.by   = celltype.col,
  group_name = target.celltype
)

# Get the full module assignment table
modules <- GetModules(seurat_obj, wgcna_name = params$wgcna.name)
head(modules)

# Get the top 10 hub genes from each module
hub_df <- GetHubGenes(seurat_obj, n_hubs = params$hub.n)
head(hub_df, 20)
```

## Visualize kME score distributions

```{r step8b_kme_plot}
# Plot the distribution of kME values across all modules
# Each panel shows one module; genes with high kME are the hub genes
p_kme <- PlotKMEs(seurat_obj, ncol = params$kme.ncol)
ggsave(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/kme_distributions.pdf"), plot = p_kme, width = 14, height = 8)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_kme)
```

## Plot harmonized module eigengenes on cells

```{r step9_hme_umap, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 9}
# Project harmonized module eigengenes onto the single-cell UMAP
# Each panel shows the activity of one module across all cells
plot_list_hme <- ModuleFeaturePlot(
  seurat_obj,
  features  = "hMEs",
  order     = TRUE,
  reduction = params$umap.reduction  # Specify the correct UMAP reduction name
)

# Verify plots were generated before saving -- stops early if ModuleFeaturePlot failed
stopifnot(length(plot_list_hme) > 0)

p_hme <- wrap_plots(plot_list_hme, ncol = params$module.plot.ncol)
ggsave(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/module_eigengene_umap.pdf"), plot = p_hme, width = 16, height = 12)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_hme)
```

## Compute and visualize single-cell module scores

```{r step10_scores, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 9}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 10: Compute and Visualize Single-Cell Module Scores
#-----------------------------------------------
# Compute module scores using the UCell algorithm
# n_genes: number of top hub genes per module to use for scoring
seurat_obj <- ModuleExprScore(
  seurat_obj,
  n_genes = params$score.n_genes,
  method  = params$score.method
)

# Plot module scores on the UMAP
plot_list_scores <- ModuleFeaturePlot(
  seurat_obj,
  features  = "scores",
  order     = TRUE,
  ucell     = TRUE,
  reduction = params$umap.reduction  # Specify the correct UMAP reduction name
)

p_scores <- wrap_plots(plot_list_scores, ncol = params$module.plot.ncol)
ggsave(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/module_scores_umap.pdf"), plot = p_scores, width = 16, height = 12)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_scores)
```

## Functional enrichment analysis

```{r step11_enrichr, eval = params$run.enrichr}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 11: Functional Enrichment Analysis
#-----------------------------------------------
# ADDED: this chunk needs internet access (Enrichr web service); it only runs
# when params$run.enrichr is TRUE.

# Define the databases to query
# Use the most up-to-date versions of GO and KEGG
dbs <- unlist(params$enrichr.dbs)

# Run enrichment analysis on all modules
seurat_obj <- RunEnrichr(
  seurat_obj,
  dbs      = dbs,
  max_genes = params$enrichr.max_genes  # Use up to 100 genes per module for enrichment
)

# Retrieve the full enrichment results table
enrich_df <- GetEnrichrTable(seurat_obj)
head(enrich_df)

# Generate bar plots of the top enriched terms for each module
# Plots are saved to the specified output directory
# FIX/ADDED: output directory placed under the project directory
enrichr.dir <- file.path(wgcna.dir, "enrichr_plots")
dir.create(enrichr.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
EnrichrBarPlot(
  seurat_obj,
  outdir     = enrichr.dir,
  n_terms    = params$enrichr.n_terms,  # Show the top 10 enriched terms per module
  plot_size  = c(params$enrichr.plot_width, params$enrichr.plot_height),  # Width x height in inches
  logscale   = TRUE                     # Plot -log10(adjusted p-value) on the x-axis
)
```

## Differential module eigengene (DME) analysis

```{r step12_dme}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 12: Differential Module Eigengene (DME) Analysis
#-----------------------------------------------
# Direct pairwise DME test: Healthy vs Post_Treatment
# Positive log2FC = higher module activity in Healthy
# Negative log2FC = higher module activity in Post_Treatment
# NOTE (article logic, kept unchanged): this test uses ALL cells of the two
# conditions, although the network was built on the target cell type only.
# Consider restricting barcodes1/barcodes2 to cells of target.celltype
# (e.g. also require seurat_obj[[celltype.col]] == target.celltype) so that
# differences reflect that cell type rather than changes in cell composition.
DMEs <- FindDMEs(
  seurat_obj,
  barcodes1  = colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj[[condition.col]][, 1] == params$dme.group1],
  barcodes2  = colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj[[condition.col]][, 1] == params$dme.group2],
  test.use   = params$dme.test,
  wgcna_name = params$wgcna.name
)

# Inspect the results table
# Columns: module, avg_ME, p_val, p_val_adj, log2FC
head(DMEs)

p_dme <- PlotDMEsVolcano(
  seurat_obj,
  DMEs       = DMEs,
  wgcna_name = params$wgcna.name
)

ggsave(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/DME_volcano.pdf"), plot = p_dme, width = 8, height = 6)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_dme)
```

## Hub gene network plot

```{r step13_hubnet}
# Plot a network graph of hub genes from all modules
# n_hubs: number of hub genes per module to include
# n_other: additional non-hub genes to include per module
# edge_prop: proportion of edges to display (0.75 = top 75% strongest connections)
# HubGeneNetworkPlot uses future.apply internally -- raise the globals size limit
options(future.globals.maxSize = params$future.maxsize.gb * 1024^3)

# HubGeneNetworkPlot renders directly to the graphics device -- use pdf() on HPC
pdf(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/hub_gene_network.pdf"), width = 10, height = 10)
HubGeneNetworkPlot(
  seurat_obj,
  n_hubs     = params$net.n_hubs,
  n_other    = params$net.n_other,
  edge_prop  = params$net.edge_prop,
  mods       = params$net.mods
)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: png twin so the plot shows in the rendered notebook
hubnet.png <- file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/hub_gene_network.png")
png(hubnet.png, width = 10, height = 10, units = "in", res = params$plot.dpi)
HubGeneNetworkPlot(
  seurat_obj,
  n_hubs     = params$net.n_hubs,
  n_other    = params$net.n_other,
  edge_prop  = params$net.edge_prop,
  mods       = params$net.mods
)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Gene co-expression network UMAP

```{r step13b_modumap}
# Build a UMAP representation of the gene co-expression network
# n_hubs: number of hub genes per module used to define the UMAP layout
seurat_obj <- RunModuleUMAP(
  seurat_obj,
  n_hubs      = params$modumap.n_hubs,
  n_neighbors = params$modumap.n_neighbors,
  min_dist    = params$modumap.min_dist
)

# Plot the gene network UMAP with ModuleUMAPPlot
# edge_prop = 0.05: show only the top 5% strongest gene-gene connections for clarity
# ModuleUMAPPlot renders directly to the graphics device -- use pdf() on HPC
pdf(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/gene_network_umap.pdf"), width = 10, height = 9)
ModuleUMAPPlot(
  seurat_obj,
  edge_prop        = params$modumap.edge_prop,
  label_hubs       = params$modumap.label_hubs,
  keep_grey_edges  = FALSE
)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: png twin so the plot shows in the rendered notebook
modumap.png <- file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/gene_network_umap.png")
png(modumap.png, width = 10, height = 9, units = "in", res = params$plot.dpi)
ModuleUMAPPlot(
  seurat_obj,
  edge_prop        = params$modumap.edge_prop,
  label_hubs       = params$modumap.label_hubs,
  keep_grey_edges  = FALSE
)
invisible(dev.off())
```

```{r step13b_show_modumap, out.width = "80%"}
# ADDED: show the base-graphics PNG saved above
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(modumap.png))
```

## Save your results

```{r step14_save}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 14: Save Your Results
#-----------------------------------------------
# Save the Seurat object with all hdWGCNA results embedded
saveRDS(seurat_obj, file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/seurat_hdwgcna.rds"))

# Export the module assignment table as a CSV
write.csv(modules, file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/monocyte_modules.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Export hub genes
write.csv(hub_df, file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/monocyte_hub_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Export DME results
write.csv(DMEs, file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/monocyte_DMEs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Export enrichment results
# ADDED: only available when the Enrichr chunk was run (params$run.enrichr)
if (exists("enrich_df")) {
  write.csv(enrich_df, file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/monocyte_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("Enrichr was not run (params$run.enrichr is FALSE); skipping monocyte_enrichment.csv")
}
```
